perf.summary: OneSixth is multiplied into volume and into each of three gradients, then squared in lengthsq; the 1/6 factors can be factored out of w and folded.
perf.currentCost: 4 separate '* OneSixth' multiplies (volume, grad1, grad2, grad3) plus grad0 sum; then w uses lengthsq of the already-scaled grads (each lengthsq re-multiplies). The 1/6 appears squared inside w and linearly in c.
perf.proposedChange: Compute raw cross products g1=cross(d2,d3), g2=cross(d3,d1), g3=cross(d1,d2), g0=-(g1+g2+g3) WITHOUT the 1/6. Then volume=dot(g1,d1)*OneSixth (or dot(cross(d1,d2),d3)*OneSixth). w_raw = invMass0*lengthsq(g0)+...; the true w = w_raw*OneSixth*OneSixth. c = volume-restVolume. lambda = -c/(w_raw*(1/36) + alpha). Final position update uses grad_i = g_i*OneSixth, i.e. delta = invMass_i*lambda*OneSixth*g_i — fold OneSixth*lambda into a scalar k once. Removes 3 vector scalings from the gradient construction.
perf.rationale: Folds four float3 scalar-multiplies into scalar constant folding (1/36 precomputed as a named const), trimming vector ALU ops on the hot path while keeping the same math.
perf.risk: Floating-point: factoring 1/6 out of squared terms changes rounding (w_raw*1/36 vs scaling-then-square). Not bit-identical. Precompute OneThirtySixth as a named const to satisfy house rules. Behavior preserved to rounding tolerance only.
